lit: what one's strength is able to reach

use.how: Mostly a modifier before 的 + noun: 做一些力所能及的事, 在力所能及的范围内. Describes tasks or help that someone can manage.

near.diff: 量力而行 is advice to act only as far as your strength allows; 力所能及 describes the tasks themselves as ones you can manage.

cue: A parent says a seven-year-old is old enough to help with small chores, such as setting the table. What kind of chores are these?

ctx.s: 孩子大了，可以让他做一些{力所能及}的家务。
ctx.en: The child is older now; you can let him do some household chores he can manage.

ctx.s: 退休以后，我想在{力所能及}的范围内帮帮社区。
ctx.en: After I retire, I want to help the community as far as I am able.

ctx.s: 有什么{力所能及}的事，您尽管吩咐。
ctx.en: If there is anything I can do, just tell me.

ctx.s: 志愿者们为受灾群众提供了{力所能及}的帮助。
ctx.en: The volunteers gave the people hit by the disaster whatever help they could.

ctx.s: 老人虽然行动不便，还是坚持做{力所能及}的工作。
ctx.en: Although the old man has trouble getting around, he still insists on doing the work he can manage.

ctx.s: 公司要求每个员工在{力所能及}的前提下参与节能活动。
ctx.en: The company asks every employee to take part in the energy-saving campaign as far as they reasonably can.

bad.s: 这座山太高了，我们{力所能及}，还是别爬了。
bad.en: (meant: this is beyond our ability)
bad.why: It means something IS within your power; for what is beyond it, Chinese says li suo bu ji or li bu cong xin.

bad.s: 他{力所能及}地跑完了全程马拉松。
bad.en: (meant: he ran the whole marathon with all his might)
bad.why: It describes tasks within reach, not an all-out effort; for giving everything you have, use quan li yi fu.

lit: to measure one's strength and then act

story.text: The phrase comes from a comment in the Zuo Zhuan on Duke Zhuang of Zheng. After Zheng and its allies took the capital of the small state of Xu, the duke did not swallow Xu up but left a member of its ruling house in charge of its people. The chronicle praises him: he weighed his virtue before taking his place and measured his strength before acting.

use.how: A predicate, very often in advice after 要 or 应该: 运动要量力而行。 Said about spending, exercise, commitments and plans.

near.diff: 力所能及 describes tasks within your power; 量力而行 is the act or advice of not going beyond your strength or budget.

cue: A friend just recovering from an injury wants to run ten kilometres on his first day back. What do you advise him?

ctx.s: 刚开始锻炼，一定要{量力而行}。
ctx.en: When you are just starting to exercise, you must not push beyond what your body can take.

ctx.s: 买房是大事，还是{量力而行}吧，别背太多贷款。
ctx.en: Buying a flat is a big deal; stay within your means and don't take on too much debt.

ctx.s: 医生说：“爬山可以，但要{量力而行}，累了就休息。”
ctx.en: The doctor said: "Hiking is fine, but don't overdo it; rest when you get tired."

ctx.s: 捐款完全自愿，大家{量力而行}就好。
ctx.en: Donations are entirely voluntary; everyone should just give what they can afford.

ctx.s: 他没有{量力而行}，一下子接了三个项目，结果都做砸了。
ctx.en: He did not know his limits, took on three projects at once, and botched them all.

ctx.s: 小公司扩张要{量力而行}，不能盲目追求规模。
ctx.en: A small company should expand only as far as its resources allow and not chase size blindly.

bad.s: 这次考试他{量力而行}，考了全班第一。
bad.en: (meant: he gave it everything and came first)
bad.why: It means holding back to stay within your limits; it does not mean trying your hardest.

bad.s: 这件事对我来说是{量力而行}的。
bad.en: (meant: this is within my ability)
bad.why: It is an action or advice, not a description of a task; for a task within your power, use li suo neng ji.

lit: calm and secure, without any illness or harm (yang is an old word for illness or trouble)

use.how: A predicate, often after 都 or 依然: 所有乘客都安然无恙。 Said of people, animals or things that came through danger or a long absence unharmed.

near.diff: 平安无事 is simply that nothing went wrong; 安然无恙 stresses coming out unharmed despite a danger or accident.

cue: A car rolls into a ditch, but the news says the driver climbed out without a scratch. How is the driver described?

ctx.s: 车翻了，幸好司机{安然无恙}。
ctx.en: The car overturned, but luckily the driver was unhurt.

ctx.s: 地震过后，他第一时间打电话确认家人{安然无恙}。
ctx.en: After the earthquake he immediately phoned to make sure his family were safe.

ctx.s: 走失了三天的小狗终于找到了，而且{安然无恙}。
ctx.en: The puppy that had been missing for three days was finally found, safe and sound.

ctx.s: “孩子们都没事吧？”“放心，都{安然无恙}。”
ctx.en: "Are the children all right?" "Don't worry, they're all safe and sound."

ctx.s: 大火烧毁了整栋楼，只有那幅古画{安然无恙}。
ctx.en: The fire destroyed the whole building; only the old painting survived undamaged.

ctx.s: 据报道，飞机紧急迫降，机上乘客全部{安然无恙}。
ctx.en: According to reports, the plane made an emergency landing and all the passengers on board were unharmed.

bad.s: 这家店的生意一直{安然无恙}，越来越红火。
bad.en: (meant: the shop's business has always gone well and keeps growing)
bad.why: It means coming through a danger or accident unharmed; it cannot describe a business doing well.

bad.s: 他今天心情{安然无恙}，一直在笑。
bad.en: (meant: he is in a calm, good mood today)
bad.why: It is about physical safety after danger, not about mood.

lit: sweat flows until it soaks the back

story.text: In the Book of the Later Han, the young Emperor Xian, a puppet of the warlord Cao Cao, once told him to his face: if you will support me, be generous; if not, do me the kindness of letting me go. Cao Cao went pale and asked to leave, and when he came out his sweat had soaked through to his back. After that he never again dared to attend court audiences.

use.how: A predicate or after 得: 热得汗流浃背。 Mostly about heat or hard physical work; also, as in the old story, about fear or deep embarrassment.

near.diff: 挥汗如雨 pictures sweat wiped off like rain during hard toil; 汗流浃背 is soaked through, and can also come from fear or shame.

cue: After carrying boxes up six floors in July with no lift, your T-shirt is stuck to your back. How do you look?

ctx.s: 天太热了，走了几步就{汗流浃背}。
ctx.en: It was so hot that after a few steps I was dripping with sweat.

ctx.s: 搬家工人扛着冰箱上楼，累得{汗流浃背}。
ctx.en: The movers carried the fridge upstairs and were soaked in sweat from the effort.

ctx.s: 你怎么{汗流浃背}的？是跑步回来的吗？
ctx.en: Why are you all sweaty? Did you run back?

ctx.s: 农民们顶着烈日在田里收麦子，个个{汗流浃背}。
ctx.en: The farmers were harvesting wheat under the blazing sun, every one of them drenched in sweat.

ctx.s: 面试官的问题一个比一个难，他紧张得{汗流浃背}。
ctx.en: The interviewer's questions got harder and harder; he was so nervous he broke out in a sweat.

ctx.s: 读完老师的批语，我惭愧得{汗流浃背}。
ctx.en: Reading the teacher's comments, I was so ashamed I broke into a cold sweat.

bad.s: 冬天的早上，他在外面冻得{汗流浃背}。
bad.en: (meant: he was shivering with cold outside on a winter morning)
bad.why: It means soaked in sweat from heat, exertion, fear or shame, never a reaction to cold.

bad.s: 下了一场大雨，他全身{汗流浃背}。
bad.en: (meant: he was soaked by the rain)
bad.why: It means wet with sweat only; being soaked by rain is hun shen shi tou.

mean: the whole range of human emotions

story.text: The four words appear together in the Doctrine of the Mean: when joy, anger, sorrow and happiness have not yet arisen, that is called balance; when they arise and each is in due measure, that is called harmony. From there the phrase came to stand for all human feelings.

use.how: A noun phrase, as subject or object: 人的喜怒哀乐, 分享喜怒哀乐, 喜怒哀乐都写在脸上. Covers all of someone's feelings, good and bad.

near.diff: 悲欢离合 is the ups and downs of life as people meet and part; 喜怒哀乐 is the emotions themselves, including anger.

cue: An actor says his job is to show the audience every feeling a person can have, from rage to delight. What does he show?

ctx.s: 他是个直性子，{喜怒哀乐}全写在脸上。
ctx.en: He is a straightforward person; every feeling he has shows on his face.

ctx.s: 好朋友就是能分享彼此{喜怒哀乐}的人。
ctx.en: Good friends are people who share each other's ups and downs.

ctx.s: 这部小说写尽了普通人的{喜怒哀乐}。
ctx.en: This novel captures every joy and sorrow of ordinary people.

ctx.s: 当演员，就要学会表达各种{喜怒哀乐}。
ctx.en: To be an actor, you have to learn to express every kind of emotion.

ctx.s: 小猫也有自己的{喜怒哀乐}吗？
ctx.en: Do cats have their own emotions too?

ctx.s: 她在日记里记录着这些年的{喜怒哀乐}。
ctx.en: In her diary she recorded all her feelings over these years.

bad.s: 听到这个好消息，大家都很{喜怒哀乐}。
bad.en: (meant: everyone was very happy)
bad.why: It is a noun naming all emotions together, not an adjective, and it does not mean only happy.

bad.s: 他是个{喜怒哀乐}的人，动不动就发脾气。
bad.en: (meant: he is a moody person who flares up easily)
bad.why: It names all feelings as a noun and cannot describe a moody person; for that, Chinese says xi nu wu chang.

mean: the joys and sorrows of meeting and parting
lit: sorrow and joy, parting and reunion

story.text: The phrase is best known from Su Shi's Mid-Autumn poem of 1076, written after a night of drinking while he missed his younger brother Su Zhe, whom he had not seen for years: people have sorrow and joy, parting and reunion; the moon is dim or bright, full or waning; this has never been perfect since ancient times. He ends by wishing they may both live long and share the moon's beauty though a thousand miles apart.
story.source: 苏轼《水调歌头·明月几时有》

use.how: A noun phrase, often object of 经历 or 看尽, or after 人生的: 人生的悲欢离合. Said of lives, families and stories with partings and reunions.

near.diff: 喜怒哀乐 is the feelings themselves; 悲欢离合 is the events of life, separations and reunions, with the sorrow and joy they bring.

cue: A family saga follows relatives scattered by war, some lost for decades, some reunited in old age. What does it portray?

ctx.s: 这部电视剧讲的是一个大家庭的{悲欢离合}。
ctx.en: This TV series tells of the partings and reunions, sorrows and joys, of a big family.

ctx.s: 在火车站工作了三十年，他看尽了人间的{悲欢离合}。
ctx.en: Having worked at the railway station for thirty years, he has seen every kind of farewell and reunion.

ctx.s: 人生总有{悲欢离合}，别太难过了。
ctx.en: Life always has its partings and reunions; don't be too sad.

ctx.s: 奶奶给我讲了她年轻时经历的{悲欢离合}。
ctx.en: Grandma told me about the separations and reunions she went through when she was young.

ctx.s: 中秋夜读苏轼的词，更能体会{悲欢离合}的滋味。
ctx.en: Reading Su Shi's poem on Mid-Autumn night, you feel more deeply what parting and reunion mean.

ctx.s: 这本书通过两兄弟的{悲欢离合}，写出了一个时代的变迁。
ctx.en: Through the separations and reunions of two brothers, the book portrays the changes of an era.

bad.s: 他今天{悲欢离合}，一会儿笑一会儿哭。
bad.en: (meant: his mood keeps swinging today)
bad.why: It is about the course of a life, meetings and partings, not mood swings within a day.

bad.s: 我们公司下午开会讨论了很多{悲欢离合}。
bad.en: (meant: we discussed many ups and downs)
bad.why: It is about people being separated and reunited, out of place for the ups and downs of a business.

lit: the interest has still not run out

use.how: A predicate or adverbial, often with 让人, 觉得 or 大家: 听完还意犹未尽。 Said after something enjoyable ends while people still want more.

near.diff: 流连忘返 is lingering in a pleasant place and not wanting to leave; 意犹未尽 is the feeling, after anything enjoyable ends, of wanting more.

cue: The concert is over and the lights are on, but the audience keeps clapping for another song. How do they feel?

ctx.s: 电影结束了，大家还{意犹未尽}。
ctx.en: The film was over, but everyone still wanted more.

ctx.s: 这本小说太好看了，读完让人{意犹未尽}。
ctx.en: This novel is so good that when you finish it you're left wanting more.

ctx.s: 讲座已经超时了，同学们却{意犹未尽}，围着教授继续提问。
ctx.en: The lecture had already run over, but the students still wanted more and gathered round the professor with questions.

ctx.s: 你看起来还{意犹未尽}啊，要不要再玩一局？
ctx.en: You look like you could keep going. Shall we play another round?

ctx.s: 老朋友聊到半夜，仍然{意犹未尽}，约好周末再聚。
ctx.en: The old friends talked until midnight and still had more to say, so they agreed to meet again at the weekend.

ctx.s: 比赛在高潮中结束，现场观众{意犹未尽}，久久不肯离场。
ctx.en: The match ended at its high point; the crowd wanted more and would not leave for a long time.

bad.s: 这部电影太无聊了，看得我{意犹未尽}。
bad.en: (meant: I couldn't wait for it to end)
bad.why: It means you enjoyed something and wanted more, the opposite of boredom.

bad.s: 他的作业还{意犹未尽}，明天再交。
bad.en: (meant: his homework is not finished yet)
bad.why: It is about lingering enjoyment, not an unfinished task; for that, simply say the homework is not done yet.

lit: loving a house extends even to the crows on its roof

story.text: After King Wu of Zhou defeated the last Shang king, he asked Jiang Taigong what to do with the conquered Shang soldiers. Taigong answered that when you love a man you love even the crow on his roof, and when you do not, you hate everything of his, so they should all be killed. The king turned to other advisers and in the end followed the gentler counsel of the Duke of Zhou. The image of the crow became the idiom.

use.how: A predicate, often explaining a reason: 他是爱屋及乌. Said when fondness for a person spreads to things or people connected with them.

near.diff: 情有独钟 is a special love for one thing in itself; 爱屋及乌 is liking something only because it belongs to someone you love.

cue: She never liked football, but since dating a keen fan she follows his team and even wears its scarf. Why?

ctx.s: 他喜欢女朋友，{爱屋及乌}，连她的猫也宠着。
ctx.en: He loves his girlfriend, and that extends even to her cat, which he spoils.

ctx.s: 奶奶疼孙子，{爱屋及乌}，对孙子的同学也特别热情。
ctx.en: Grandma dotes on her grandson, so she is especially warm to his classmates too.

ctx.s: 因为喜欢这位作家，我{爱屋及乌}，去了他的家乡旅游。
ctx.en: Because I love this writer, I even took a trip to his home town.

ctx.s: 你对我弟弟这么好，是不是{爱屋及乌}啊？
ctx.en: You're so nice to my little brother. Is it because of me?

ctx.s: 很多球迷{爱屋及乌}，连球星代言的饮料都买。
ctx.en: Many fans extend their love to everything around their idol, even buying the drinks the star advertises.

ctx.s: 岳父母对女婿好，往往是{爱屋及乌}，因为疼爱女儿。
ctx.en: Parents-in-law who are good to a son-in-law often do it for their daughter's sake.

bad.s: 他特别爱自己的房子，真是{爱屋及乌}。
bad.en: (meant: he really loves his house)
bad.why: The house is only the image; it means love for a person spreading to what is theirs.

bad.s: 我从小就{爱屋及乌}，最喜欢画画。
bad.en: (meant: I have loved painting since childhood)
bad.why: Love for one thing in itself is qing you du zhong; this idiom needs a person whose belongings you love.

mean: to have a special fondness for one thing
lit: one's feelings gather on one thing alone

use.how: Usually 对……情有独钟: 他对老电影情有独钟。 Said of a lasting preference for one thing, place, style or person over others.

near.diff: 爱屋及乌 is liking something because of someone you love; 情有独钟 is loving one thing for itself, more than all others.

cue: Your friend has tried every kind of tea, yet for twenty years she has drunk only one green tea from her home province. How would you put it?

ctx.s: 我对川菜{情有独钟}，每周都要吃一次。
ctx.en: I have a soft spot for Sichuan food; I have to eat it once a week.

ctx.s: 他走过很多城市，却唯独对杭州{情有独钟}。
ctx.en: He has been to many cities, but Hangzhou is the one he loves above all.

ctx.s: 你为什么对这个牌子的手表{情有独钟}？
ctx.en: Why are you so attached to this brand of watch?

ctx.s: 不少年轻人对复古风格的衣服{情有独钟}。
ctx.en: Quite a few young people have a special fondness for vintage-style clothes.

ctx.s: 在所有乐器中，她对钢琴{情有独钟}。
ctx.en: Of all instruments, the piano is the one she loves most.

ctx.s: 这位导演对小人物的故事一直{情有独钟}。
ctx.en: This director has always had a special interest in stories about ordinary people.

bad.s: 他对所有运动都{情有独钟}。
bad.en: (meant: he loves all sports)
bad.why: Du means one alone: it singles out one favourite, so it cannot apply to everything.

bad.s: 我昨天{情有独钟}地吃了一碗面。
bad.en: (meant: I enjoyed a bowl of noodles yesterday)
bad.why: It is a lasting preference, used in the pattern dui ... qing you du zhong, not a way of doing a one-off action.

mean: longing to get home as fast as possible
lit: the heart set on returning is like an arrow

use.how: A predicate, often after 早已 or 个个: 春节快到了，大家都归心似箭。 Said of people away from home, typically before holidays or at the end of a long trip.

near.diff: 迫不及待 is impatience for anything at all; 归心似箭 is specifically the eagerness to get back home.

cue: A migrant worker who has not seen his family all year packs his bag a week before the Spring Festival train leaves. How does he feel?

ctx.s: 快过年了，在外打工的人都{归心似箭}。
ctx.en: New Year is nearly here, and everyone working away from home is longing to get back.

ctx.s: 出差一个月，我早就{归心似箭}了。
ctx.en: I've been on a business trip for a month; I've long been desperate to get home.

ctx.s: 毕业典礼一结束，留学多年的她就{归心似箭}，订了最早的航班。
ctx.en: As soon as the graduation ceremony was over, she, after years of studying abroad, was desperate to get home and booked the earliest flight.

ctx.s: “下班了还不走？”“走！老婆孩子在等我，我{归心似箭}啊。”
ctx.en: "Not leaving yet?" "I'm off! My wife and kids are waiting; I can't get home fast enough."

ctx.s: 春运期间，火车站里挤满了{归心似箭}的旅客。
ctx.en: During the Spring Festival travel rush, the stations are packed with travellers eager to get home.

ctx.s: 战士们完成任务，{归心似箭}，连夜往回赶。
ctx.en: The soldiers finished their mission and, eager to return, hurried back through the night.

bad.s: 他{归心似箭}，想快点出国旅游。
bad.en: (meant: he can't wait to travel abroad)
bad.why: It is eagerness to return home, not to leave for somewhere new.

bad.s: 这支箭飞得{归心似箭}，一下就射中了靶心。
bad.en: (meant: the arrow flew very fast)
bad.why: The arrow is only a comparison for a homesick heart; it does not describe real speed.
